newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta shrugs aside sharp bond, equity drops.
newsitem.headline: Peseta shrugs aside sharp bond, equity drops.

text.p: The peseta traded serenely in the first session of 1997 on Thursday, ignoring the sharp correction in the Spanish debt and equity markets.
The strong drop on Wall Street, and the fall in U.S. Treasury markets hit the dollar, and pressed shares and bonds lower. But the peseta held aloof.
"It's an all-around correction in the bond and share markets after the euphoria before the end of the year and there is no particular reason for it to affect the peseta," a dealer said.
Despite the bond fall, the bono/Bund spread narrowed to an historic low beneath 100 basis points.
One dealer said the bond correction must be far sharper and prompt a rise in the spread before the peseta was shaken from its trading range of recent months between 84.00/84.40 per mark.
At 1610 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.29/31 after opening at 84.29/32.
